static-spa.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages. No rewrite. Drop your build output (dist/, out/, build/) in via `wrangler pages deploy` or the GitHub integration.
caveats: If you use service workers, verify that Pages serves them with the right Cache-Control.
_redirects and _headers control routing/headers — both are first-class on Pages.

nextjs.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages or Workers via @cloudflare/next-on-pages or OpenNext for Cloudflare. Pick @cloudflare/next-on-pages for App Router projects on edge runtime; OpenNext for projects that need full Node compatibility.
caveats: ISR / on-demand revalidation requires the right adapter — verify your data-fetching modes.
next/image needs the Cloudflare Images binding or an unoptimized loader.
Edge runtime vs Node runtime split: every route file must declare `export const runtime = 'edge'` to deploy to Workers.
Server Actions are supported but should sit behind a rate-limit rule.

astro.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages with @astrojs/cloudflare adapter. Static + hybrid + server modes all supported.
caveats: If you use Astro DB, that's libSQL — separate path from D1; do not assume they're interchangeable.

sveltekit.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages with @sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare. Workers deploy supported via @sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare-workers.
caveats: form actions are POST-heavy — check rate-limit-rules.starter.json covers them.

remix.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages or Workers with the Remix Cloudflare templates. Use the new Vite plugin path for greenfield projects.
caveats: Loaders/actions run on the edge by default — long-running side effects need to move to a Worker queue or Durable Object.

nuxt.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages or Workers with `nuxt build --preset=cloudflare-pages` or `cloudflare`.
caveats: Nuxt's Nitro engine handles the abstraction; verify your Nitro modules are edge-compatible.

solidstart.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages with the SolidStart Cloudflare preset. SSR + static both supported.

vite-spa.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages — drop the dist/ output. Pure static, no SSR needed.

hono.recommended_path: Workers, no rewrite. Hono's Cloudflare adapter is the canonical path; `wrangler deploy` is the only command needed.

itty-router.recommended_path: Workers, no rewrite. itty-router is Cloudflare-native.

workers-native.recommended_path: Already on Workers. Skill focuses on hardening (wrangler.hardened.toml + secrets migration).

express.recommended_path: Often rewritable to Workers via Hono or a thin compat shim, but only after auditing dependencies. If you depend on long-lived TCP, native modules, or Node-only APIs, plan for Containers (beta) or keep on origin behind Cloudflare proxy.
caveats: express middleware that uses Buffer extensively or streams large files needs review.
Sessions in memory don't survive Workers — move to KV / Durable Objects / Hyperdrive-backed Postgres.

fastify.recommended_path: Same as Express. Fastify's plugin model often makes the rewrite to Hono/Workers more mechanical, but the dependency audit is identical.
caveats: fastify-multipart streaming uploads → R2 multipart upload via Workers.

nestjs.recommended_path: Larger surface than Express/Fastify. NestJS's DI + decorators don't run on Workers without significant adapter work. Honest path: keep on origin behind Cloudflare proxy + Tunnel; or use Containers (beta).
caveats: Microservices via TCP/Redis transports won't run on Workers.
TypeORM / Sequelize generally won't work on Workers — switch to Drizzle or a Worker-compatible client + Hyperdrive.

static-html.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages. Drop the directory; done.

hugo.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages with the Hugo build preset. Build command: `hugo --minify`. Output: `public/`.

jekyll.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages with the Jekyll build preset. Output: `_site/`.

eleventy.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages. Output: `_site/` or `dist/` depending on config.

gatsby.recommended_path: Cloudflare Pages. Gatsby outputs `public/`. Note Gatsby Cloud is sunset; this is a real migration off, not a lateral move.
caveats: Gatsby Functions don't have a 1:1 mapping — port to Pages Functions or Workers.

wordpress.recommended_path: Don't try to run WordPress on Workers. Keep your origin where it is. Put Cloudflare in front: DNS → proxied → free WAF + DDoS + CDN + Tunnel to hide the origin's public IP. Consider headless WP + a JS frontend later if the static gain matters.
caveats: wp-admin, xmlrpc.php, wp-cron.php should be IP-allowlisted or behind Access.
Authenticated Origin Pulls + a Tunnel removes the public origin entirely.

laravel.recommended_path: PHP doesn't run on Workers. Cloudflare in front of the origin gets you the security/perf wins for free. Containers (beta) may help if you're Docker-native and want to consolidate.
caveats: Laravel queue workers stay on the origin host or move to Containers.

symfony.recommended_path: Same as Laravel. Proxy + Tunnel + WAF. Containers if you want to consolidate hosting.

rails.recommended_path: Don't replatform Rails to Workers. Put Cloudflare in front of the existing origin (proxy + Tunnel + WAF + CDN). If you want Cloudflare-native compute, Containers (beta) is the only realistic path.
caveats: ActionCable WebSockets don't migrate to Workers — Durable Objects is a different model.
ActiveJob workers stay on the origin or Containers.

django.recommended_path: Same shape as Rails. Proxy + Tunnel + WAF; Containers if Docker-native.
caveats: Channels (WebSockets) don't migrate cleanly.

fastapi.recommended_path: Same as Flask. Proxy + Tunnel + WAF. Honest assessment: Python doesn't run on Workers.

spring-boot.recommended_path: JVM doesn't run on Workers. Containers or stay on origin behind Cloudflare proxy.

dotnet.recommended_path: ASP.NET / .NET doesn't run on Workers. Containers or stay on origin behind Cloudflare proxy.

go-monolith.recommended_path: Small Go services can sometimes be ported to Workers via WASM, but it's rarely worth the rewrite for a monolith. Prefer Containers (beta) or proxy-only.

media-processing-heavy.recommended_path: FFmpeg / headless browsers / ImageMagick at scale don't run on Workers. Orchestrate from Workers (queue + bindings) but keep the actual compute on R2 + Containers (beta) or external host.
caveats: Browser Rendering API may cover the headless-Chrome use cases — check the catalog before discarding.

mysql-app.recommended_path: Workers + Hyperdrive in front of your existing MySQL is the lowest-risk path — origin DB stays where it is. D1 is SQLite, NOT MySQL — moving to D1 is a full rewrite.
caveats: AUTO_INCREMENT vs AUTOINCREMENT, ENUM, TEXT vs CLOB, ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, full-text search, stored procedures, triggers — all different in SQLite/D1.
Connection string belongs in `wrangler secret put`, never `[vars]`.

postgres-app.recommended_path: Hyperdrive in front of your existing Postgres (Supabase, Neon, RDS, self-hosted). D1 is SQLite, NOT Postgres — full rewrite if you want D1.
caveats: pgBouncer transaction-pooling mode interacts with prepared statements — review the Hyperdrive docs.
Connection string belongs in `wrangler secret put`.

mongodb-app.recommended_path: Cloudflare doesn't host MongoDB. Keep MongoDB Atlas (or your existing Mongo). Workers can talk to it via the Atlas Data API or a TCP-socket-compatible driver.
caveats: Driver-over-TCP-sockets needs Workers TCP socket support and is heavier than the Data API.
Latency tradeoff: edge Worker → MongoDB Atlas region → back to user.

redis-app.recommended_path: Either keep external Redis (e.g., Upstash REST or Redis Cloud over TCP sockets) or replace with KV (eventually consistent) or Durable Objects (strong consistency, atomic counters).
caveats: KV's ~60s propagation is fine for session stores, NOT fine for atomic counters.
Durable Objects = the right answer for per-key state machines, presence, rate limits.

websocket-heavy.recommended_path: Durable Objects host WebSocket sessions natively. Works well for chat, presence, collab. Plan flags duration limits and pricing model — long-lived connections bill on duration.
caveats: 32-MB DO memory ceiling per object.
Hibernation API reduces idle cost — check whether your protocol fits.

long-running-compute.recommended_path: Workers max CPU is 30s per invocation (5min on Workers Unbound, but still bounded). For multi-minute compute, use Containers (beta) or keep on origin.

s3-storage.recommended_path: R2 — same S3 API, zero egress fees. Migrate via `rclone sync s3:bucket r2:bucket` or `aws s3 sync ... --endpoint-url=https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. Cutover order: dual-write window → switch reads → stop writes to S3 → archive S3.
caveats: S3-specific features that R2 doesn't have: lifecycle for storage classes (R2 has one class), some IAM granularity differences, S3 Select.
Public bucket access on R2 uses custom domains or `.r2.dev` — verify CORS for browser uploads.
